To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
endothelial SMAD4 signaling is required for BMP9-induced suppression of PI3K/Akt activation and inhibition of CK2 expression, which prevents AVM formation.
SMAD4 is essential for BMP-ALK1 signaling in the endothelium, and loss of endothelial SMAD4 results in arteriovenous-malformation (AVM) formation in response to high blood-flow in developing tissues.

(1) SMAD4 is required for BMP9-induced AVM prevention, (2) loss of SMAD4 causes AVMs in the retina and other tissues, (3) SMAD4 prevents AVMs by inhibiting casein kinase 1 (CK1) expression and activity, and (4) loss of SMADI causes AVMs via increased AKT1 activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathogenesis of AVMs, a common vascular disease that can lead to severe bleeding.
the molecular and genetic mechanisms that underlie the formation of AVMs
the pathogenesis of AVMs in the retina.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SMAD4 is required for BMP9/10-ALK1 effects in preventing flow-induced PI3K/Akt signaling in endothelial cells.
endothelial-specific loss of SMAD4 in mice causes AVM formation, and that SMAD4 prevents AVM formation by limiting CK2-mediated PTEN phosphorylation.
SMAD4 prevents flow induced arteriovenous Malformation by inhibiting casein Kinase 1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
endothelial SMAD4 prevents flow-induced AVMs by inhibiting CK2 and thus limiting PI3K/Akt activation.
loss of endothelium-specific SMAD4 results in AVM formation, a process that is dependent on increased endothelial AKT activation.
loss of endothelium-specific SMAD4 in adult mice causes AVMs that develop in regions with high flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SMAD4 is an essential downstream effector of BMP/ALK1 signaling in endothelial cells.
SMAD4 is an essential effector for BMP9-10 induced ALK1 signaling.
SMAD4 is an essential effector in the BMP9-10-ALK1 pathway.
